about: Chinmay's decisions of 2 October 2026 on the open questions, one row per decision, with what was decided and why. Read by tools/build-audit-decisions.py, which writes docs/registers/decisions-2-october.md. Copied into the package on 2 October (CHG-DOC-019) from the apply ledger, so the package, not the audit working folder, carries the decision log. Chinmay's own words are in docs/active/decisions/answers-2-october.md (later sections override earlier ones); the non-critical defaults he did not review are listed in docs/active/decisions/questions-defaults-to-review.md; the research cited is in docs/active/research/.
inputs: TICVAI - Open Questions (2 Oct).xlsx, sheet 'Open questions' (538 rows; workbook_q is its '#')

status_values.to-apply: decided; applied by the change entries that cite the id
status_values.already-applied: decided earlier and already in the package (applied_by)
status_values.needs-research: decided to research first; nothing applied until the research lands
status_values.needs-client: needs the client or a vendor; nothing applied until it arrives
status_values.applied: decided and applied: applied_by names the closed change entries that applied it

amends.change: One managed provider (Azure OpenAI) becomes a per-tenant AI residency class: UAE-only (default) runs on Core42 Compass through openaiCompatible, OpenAI UAE then in-cell gpt-oss-120b as fallback; Global allowed opts in under PDPL Art. 23; on-prem runs open models. The UAE-only Small tier moves to Azure UAE North PTU near 100,000 calls a day.
"UAE North for now" is replaced by the residency class: in-UAE inference by default, Global only where the tenant opts in.
Fitness "warns, never blocks" is overturned: a model outside TICVAI's curated map for the task is refused.
Closed: with BYOK the engine maps each task to the provider's curated equivalent tier; usage is billed to the client's own key.
TICVAI curates a range per AI and ML task: the best model plus 3-4 alternatives; platform-owned models are never BYOK; money paths stay classical ML.
Amended: the per-tenant residency class; the transfer register lists every Global-allowed tenant; vendor terms in writing before signing.

Amended: every LLM call passes a mandatory offline PII scrubber (Presidio with UAE and Arabic recognisers, reversible tokens) and an in-cell guard model (Qwen3Guard) on input and output, whatever the residency class.

Amended: consent first on the venue's form, with a warning where TICVAI holds the data; enrolment at the app, the counters and a kiosk, never the turnstile; minors with guardian consent, configurable; images only behind a logged, permissioned view; face matching for accreditation duplicates only with consent and the venue's legal sign-off.
Open: retention periods per data category and region wait for research into UAE and GCC law, then counsel.
Rationale recorded: F&B owns its own catalogue table (F&B prices migrated into F&B) so ticketing scales in isolation.

The outlet-scoped settings decided on 2 October: payment timing, inside the venue or standalone, outlet type and department, the till layout with a till override, the producing outlet, the default kitchen station.

Configuration is promoted to production as a versioned package (diff, approval, idempotent upsert by key, rollback by re-applying the previous package); schema goes forward only, expand then contract.
"Direction is fixed per access point" is amended: a gate's direction can be switched live with a specific permission, and the switch is logged.
"Send to kitchen, then charge" becomes an outlet setting, Payment timing: Pay first, or Send to kitchen first then pay.
The 410 workshop-pack console screens move to Venue Management; console screens that act on a tenant get the tenant picker and grant; platform staff may publish a hosted tenant's site under a grant.
Waste joins the approval list as a policy the venue switches on or off (value bands, a photo above a value).
Minors' Face Pass: guardian consent on the venue's form, the minor age per country, and the venue can switch minors off.
The kiosk is the exception: tickets first, then date and time.
The five POS v2 candidates left undecided on 1 October (POS-000, -003, -004, -012, -023) are accepted as drawn in v2.
"No F&B without an admission ticket" holds inside the venue; a standalone outlet sells without a ticket.
One cart, one receipt does not apply to F&B: the F&B order keeps its own payment step and receipt.
"Powered by TICVAI shown consistently" becomes a toggle, default on.
The cookie scanner is bought (a scanner API, hybrid); the manual upload path stays.

decisions.source: batch 2 / workbook Q#1 / ADM-037 (block A)
decisions.decision: With BYOK, the AI engine maps each AI task to the client provider's equivalent model from TICVAI's curated range (tiers, not model names: research section 2.3); usage is billed to the client's own key. Closes AI-D20 (deferred to the AI workshop).
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct (batch 2): "BYOK: the agent assigns the provider's equivalent models from TICVAI's curated range per task". Question: Who pays when a client picks its own provider or a costlier model? Drawn default was: Deferred to the AI workshop (AI-D20); until then managed Azure OpenAI in UAE North, re-billed per token, is the default and the screen shows no billing choice. Source: MoM 30 Sep 4.1 (AI-D20) | ADR-0020 (AI-D02) | ADR-0020 (AI-D03) | MoM 30 Sep 4.1.
decisions.adr_or_hld: AI-D20 (closed by this decision); ai-system-design 5.9; ADR-0009 section 3 (any BYOK provider other than OpenAI UAE is a cross-border transfer, so BYOK fits the Global-allowed residency class only)
decisions.prevention_hint: A check (extend check-contract-shapes or add check-ai-curation) that every BYOK provider kind resolves each taskKey to a curated tier; a BYOK enablement with an unmapped task fails.

decisions.decision: A client cannot change the model per agent. TICVAI curates the model for each task; setAiProvider/setAiModel refuse a model outside the curated map for that task (new problem type, e.g. modelNotCurated). Overturns AI-D18's 'warns, never blocks'.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct (batch 2): "No: the client cannot change models; TICVAI curates them (cheaper models would break the AI functions)". Question: How much may a client change the pre-selected model per agent itself? Drawn default was: Only through BYOK where TICVAI enabled it; every change logged. Source: DI-967 | MoM 21 Sep §6.
decisions.adr_or_hld: AI-D18 amended (fitness band now blocks outside the curated map); ai-system-design section 8 row 13
decisions.prevention_hint: setAiProvider and setAiModel declare the 4xx modelNotCurated response (a description promising a refusal must carry the response code; check-package); ADM-037 copy no longer says 'You can still save'.

decisions.decision: Cookie scanner: buy a scanner API (hybrid). Our banner, runtime, registry and consent logs stay; a bought scanner API feeds recordCookieScan; the manual 'Upload scan report' path stays.

decisions.prevention_hint: The integration register lists the scanner adaptor; recordCookieScan's source enum includes the vendor API value; check-cited-sources once the research file is in git.

decisions.source: batch 5 / workbook Q#168 / ADM-122 (block B)
decisions.decision: Industry standard for production change: never merge or reverse-migrate production databases. Schema goes forward-only through versioned migrations (expand then contract). Configuration moves as a versioned package exported with stable keys, diffed against production, approved, applied as an idempotent upsert by key, and audited; rollback re-applies the previous package. Secrets and environment settings never travel in it.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct (batch 5): "Industry standard: forward-only migrations; config packages with diff, approval and idempotent upsert". Question: After go-live, is configuration promoted from pre-production to production only as configuration? Drawn default was: Show transfers as configuration-only jobs with approval. Source: TRACKER Actions row 284.
decisions.adr_or_hld: New ADR (config promotion); relates to ADR-0039 (tenant database lifecycle)
decisions.ambiguity: Sent to Chinmay as 'default unless he objects'.
decisions.prevention_hint: check-migrations / check-migration-freeze already enforce forward-only schema; add a check that config-package keys are stable (check-key-stability).

decisions.source: AI residency (Chinmay, 2 Oct)
decisions.decision: Per-tenant AI residency class. UAE-only (default; mandatory for government, bank and health tenants): Small = Core42 Compass GPT-4.1 mini (or Seraj if it wins the Arabic golden set), Strong = Compass GPT-5, fallback OpenAI UAE then in-cell gpt-oss-120b. Global allowed (private venue opts in under PDPL Art. 23 with vendor contract, DPIA and notice): Azure gpt-5-mini / gpt-6-sol Global or the tenant's BYOK provider, fallback the UAE-only chain. On-prem: Qwen3.5 or gpt-oss; Strong Qwen3.5-122B, Falcon-H1 Arabic or Jais 2. Compass is reached through AiProviderKind openaiCompatible. Amends AI-D02.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct (AI residency table). Research: Azure UAE North serves no chat model in-region on pay-per-token; UAE apps use Core42/OpenAI UAE or make no claim.
decisions.adr_or_hld: AI-D02 and ADR-0009 (residency); ADR-0020; HLD/LLD residency
decisions.prevention_hint: A gateway check: a call for a UAE-only tenant can only resolve to an in-UAE endpoint (provider-region allow-list per class); ADR-0009 transfer register lists every Global-allowed tenant.

keys: 3 Cross-border AI (transfer register lists Global-allowed tenants)
tenant AI residency class (new; extends RegionSettings.allowedAiResidencies)

decisions.source: AI residency (Chinmay, 2 Oct): scale step
decisions.decision: Move the UAE-only Small tier to Azure UAE North PTU (spillover off) when steady traffic nears about 100,000 calls a day.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct (AI residency). Research 2A: pay-per-token beats PTU until near the regional ceiling; PTU starts at ~USD 8.5k/month.
decisions.prevention_hint: An observability alert on Small-tier calls/day per region (threshold ~100k) names the PTU step.

decisions.source: AI residency (Chinmay, 2 Oct): before signing
decisions.decision: Get in writing before signing: Core42 Compass terms (retention, logging, sub-processors, minimums, per-model region), OpenAI UAE approval (and Modified Abuse Monitoring), Microsoft PTU calculator figures, and legal advice on whether Miral and Dubai Holding count as government entities.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct (AI residency: 'to get in writing before signing'). Research section 4 'Not confirmed'.
decisions.prevention_hint: external-dependencies lists each item with an owner and date; the residency ADR amendment stays 'Accepted, vendor terms pending' until they arrive.

keys: Core42, OpenAI UAE, Microsoft PTU, legal opinion

decisions.source: PII scrubbing (Chinmay, 2 Oct)
decisions.decision: Every LLM call, whatever the tenant's residency class, first passes an offline scrubber inside our cell: Microsoft Presidio with custom recognisers (Emirates ID, UAE phone, passport, IBAN, Luhn-checked card, email) plus an Arabic NER model (e.g. CAMeL Tools); detected PII becomes reversible placeholders ([GUEST_1]) whose map stays in-cell, and replies are re-filled before reaching the user. Scrubbing is mandatory, not tied to residency.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct: 'we may need to scrub personal info no matter what: an offline NLP-based scrubber or censorship'. Reinforces the rule that the LLM never reads raw data (ADR-0020, masking fails closed).
decisions.prevention_hint: A gateway test corpus (Arabic and English) with Emirates IDs, phones, IBANs and cards: no raw value may appear in the outbound prompt; scrubber unavailable = call refused (fail closed).

keys: 2 Inference is a call out (amend: mandatory offline scrubbing)
gateway scrubbing policy (mandatory; ai.policy.maskedFields extended to recogniser set)

decisions.source: PII scrubbing (Chinmay, 2 Oct): moderation
decisions.decision: An offline guard model (Qwen3Guard, covers Arabic) runs on both input and output of every LLM call.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct (PII scrubbing item 3). Research section 4 item 6: Azure Content Safety's harm models are not trained on Arabic.
decisions.prevention_hint: Golden set includes Arabic harmful prompts; the guard runs in-cell (no egress).

decisions.source: Batch 2 #7 / batch 3 (AI/ML model selection)
decisions.decision: TICVAI keeps a curated range per AI and ML task: the best-suited model plus 3-4 alternatives where they exist (generative tiers Small/Strong/Reasoning; platform-owned embeddings, reranking, moderation, PII, OCR, speech never BYOK; money paths stay classical ML). Record the range in the AI design and seed it in the AI model catalogue.
decisions.why: Chinmay, 2 Oct, batch 2 #7: 'select the models now, with 3-4 options'; batch 3: 'not just AI/LLM models: ML models too'. Research delivered 2 Oct.
decisions.ambiguity: Chinmay decided to curate and asked for the picks; the individual picks (e.g. Qwen3-Embedding over BGE-M3, Qwen3-Reranker, Chronos-2 challenger) are research recommendations he has not confirmed one by one.
decisions.prevention_hint: A check that every taskKey in the AI contract has a curated tier and at least one alternative in the seed.

decisions.decision: Every tenant gets a platform subdomain at provisioning, one stem per cell (venue.<cell>.ticvai.app, e.g. *.ae.ticvai.app) with a wildcard certificate; host-only cookies; start the Public Suffix List submission.

decisions.source: Batch 5 set 2 (domains)
decisions.decision: Custom domains: a CNAME (e.g. tickets.venue.com) straight to our Front Door endpoint, validated by TXT _dnsauth, with a Front Door managed certificate. A delegated subdomain as an option; the apex only on request; no path proxy. CMS-017 gains the DNS records list (TXT, CNAME, CAA/NS with observed value and status), the pending-revalidation and timeout states, the takeover warning on release, a primary domain with redirects, and per-domain readiness (UAE Pass redirect, Apple Pay domain, app links).
decisions.why: Chinmay, batch 5: 'Subdomain plus CNAME'; batch 2 #41 and batch 3 (DNS options; check CMS-017 covers the guest web app: it does, kind guestWeb).
decisions.prevention_hint: check-states: active -> pendingRevalidation -> active; a scheduled job flags active domains whose CNAME no longer resolves to us (takeover); F103 has hostname-taken, wrong record, timeout and revalidation branches.

later_rounds.topic: No self-hosted model; the guard is the provider's safety service
later_rounds.decision: We host no model unless a client asks: no in-cell open model (gpt-oss-120b) and no GPU node pool. The AI goes through providers: Core42 Compass by default, OpenAI UAE as fallback, BYOK. The guard (Qwen3Guard) becomes the provider-side safety service (e.g. Azure AI Content Safety, UAE North; the provider's own moderation for BYOK and globalAllowed), still fail-closed. The Presidio scrubber stays as a CPU library in our own worker; scrubbing stays mandatory. On-prem or self-hosted models only when a client asks.
later_rounds.why: Chinmay, 3 October evening: "We are not hosting anything unless client asks it"; a guard model is itself an LLM (docs/active/decisions/answers-3-october-gate-and-hosting.md).
